notes: ONE CHEQUE CAN NOW PAY TWO REMITTANCE RUNS, AND THE REGISTER WILL SAY SO. When you remit withholdings and type a cheque number the register already holds, the app used to refuse it and send you to a fresh number. If you had in fact written ONE cheque covering both runs, you wrote it anyway — and the register kept only the first run's figure. From that month on, unpresented cheques were understated by the difference, and the reconciliation could only be signed off by forcing it with an adjustment. Now the app ASKS. It shows you what that number already stands for, to whom, and what the register will read if these deductions are added. Say yes and the register holds what the cheque really paid. Say no and nothing is posted — it tells you to enter the number of the cheque actually written. It never decides this for you, because a repeated number is also exactly what a typing slip looks like. EACH DEDUCTION KEEPS ITS OWN WITHHOLDING CERTIFICATE — its own payee, its own TIN, its own amount, printable separately as before. Certificates follow the person the money was withheld from, never the cheque. YOU CAN NOW CORRECT A CHEQUE'S REGISTERED AMOUNT. Cheque Register → CORRECT AMOUNT, on any cheque that is not cancelled. It asks what the cheque was actually written for — offering the figure your own remittance records say it settled — and why, which goes on the audit trail. This changes the REGISTER ONLY. No ledger entry is made, because in this situation the ledger is already right: every pesewa left the bank correctly, and it was the register that was short. Use it to put right any cheque entered before this release. AND THE APP NOW TELLS YOU WHEN THE TWO DISAGREE. The alert banner compares what your remittance records say each cheque settled against what the cheque register holds, and names any cheque where they differ. This release adds a database change, so please take a backup before upgrading.
